title: Multi-language SDK Starter Templates with Robust Retries & Streaming Ergonomics
creator: Ava Montrose
description: Create a set of opinionated, production-ready starter templates and cookbook snippets for Redwood SDK users in TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), Go (HTTP server), and a multi-platform CLI. The artifacts should showcase best-practice retry/backoff policies, idempotency guidance, streaming ergonomics (client-side and server-friendly patterns), and minimal example apps that developers can clone and run in <30 minutes. Focus goals: (1) make streaming easy and consistent across languages, (2) provide safe default retry behavior tuned for inference latency profiles, (3) include clear examples for resume/reconnect and partial result handling, and (4) ship docs + integration tests. This ticket covers templates, cookbook pages, CI test harness, and two initial code review passes. Do not duplicate prior starter kit wording; emphasize ergonomic client APIs (async iterators / readable streams / channels) and pragmatic server examples for FastAPI and Go.
acceptance_criteria: Next.js TypeScript template demonstrating streaming completion rendering via EventSource or native fetch streaming, with token-level progress UI and graceful retry on transient failure
FastAPI example showing async streaming endpoint using Redwood Python SDK with a context manager based reconnect/resume helper and documented idempotency guidance
Go HTTP server template with an efficient handler that uses the Go SDK stream reader, demonstrates per-request idempotency-key header, and integrates with net/http gracefully
Cross-platform CLI (Go/TS/Python) example that shows non-interactive streaming output and a --retry-policy flag to exercise retries in CI
Cookbook page with 6 short snippets (retry backoff, jitter, idempotency, reconnect/resume, binary streaming, structured output parsing) and unit tests for each snippet
Automated integration tests in CI that run each template against a local dev sandbox and assert expected behaviors for streaming and retry metrics
Docs: README for each template with run instructions, example outputs, and troubleshooting tips; example PRs and links included in ticket

implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): Build skeleton templates for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, and CLI. Minimal README and run scripts.

Phase 2 (Week 2): Implement robust retry helpers (exponential backoff + full jitter), idempotency-key utils, and streaming helpers (async iterator for Python, ReadableStream wrapper for TS, io.Reader-based streamer for Go).
Phase 3 (Week 3): Add integration tests in CI, polish docs, and conduct a lightweight UX dev-run to measure time-to-hello and surface errors.
Phase 4 (Week 4): Address feedback from PM, Docs, and Security; merge PRs and prepare release notes for sdk-2026.03
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Stream semantics differ across runtimes (node fetch vs browser vs Python async). Mitigation: provide both browser and Node examples for TS and a shared anti-pattern section.

Risk: Excessive retries could amplify load on serving runtime. Mitigation: default retry policy set to conservative limits (max 3 attempts, capped total backoff 10s) and documented per-environment knobs.
Risk: Templates might become stale as SDK surface changes. Mitigation: add an automated smoke test in CI that exercises the templates on each SDK release and flags regressions.

Risk: Private deployment secrets handling differs. Mitigation: add explicit guidance in READMEs for KMS/HSM and environment variable patterns; mark the FastAPI and Go templates with a 'private-deploy' note.
testing_plan: Unit tests for retry helpers (simulate transient 500s, verify backoff timing and max attempts)
Integration test that runs each template in a lightweight Docker container against a local dev server stub that can inject failures and resume tokens
End-to-end runbook that an engineer follows to create a new template from scratch in <1 hour; include checklist items
Hook into SDK e2e pipeline to run templates on nightly and post results to #sdk-templates Slack channel
